They should use the existing verification, login, profile, and recovery flows.

A customer opens a request like this:

```http
POST /api/v1/requests

{"request":{"subject":"Cannot download my receipt","comment":{"body":"The download button does nothing."}}}
```

Return it inside `request`, with its ID, subject, status, requester ID, and timestamps. A new
request is open. Customers can list their own requests, open one, and read its comments at
`/requests`, `/requests/:id`, and `/requests/:id/comments`. Staff have the corresponding `/tickets`
routes; return records inside `ticket` there and include the requester as `{"id":10,"name":"Avery","email":"avery@example.test"}`.
Lists use the plural resource name. Comments include their body, author (`id` and `name`), whether
they're `public`, and when they were created.

Replies go through PATCH. For example, the owner can answer and mark a ticket pending:

```http
PATCH /api/v1/tickets/42

{"ticket":{"comment":{"body":"Please try again now."},"status":"pending"}}
```

Customers reply through `/requests/:id` with the `request` envelope. Customer replies reopen pending
or solved requests unless they mark the request solved in the same update. Staff can choose open, pending,
or solved. Posting a staff reply by itself doesn't change the status.

Paginate lists with `page` and `per_page` (default 1 and 25), returning `count`, `page`, `per_page`,
`next_page`, and `previous_page` alongside the records. Show recently active tickets and requests
first, and comments oldest first. This is a portal-only conversation for now; replies don't send email.

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Api
  module V1
    class AccountsController < BaseController
      before_action :require_account!, only: %i[show cancel reactivate]
      before_action :authenticate_user!, only: %i[show cancel reactivate]
      before_action :require_active_account!, only: %i[show]
      before_action :require_owner!, only: %i[cancel reactivate]

      def create
        account_params = require_hash_param(params, :account)
        admin_params = require_hash_param(account_params, :admin)

        account = Account.new(account_params.permit(:name, :subdomain))
        user = User.new(
          admin_params.permit(:name, :email, :password).merge(account: account, role: "admin")
        )

        account_valid = account.valid?
        user_valid = user.valid?

        unless account_valid && user_valid
          errors = account.errors.to_hash
          errors[:admin] = user.errors.to_hash if user.errors.any?
          render_validation_errors(errors)
          return
        end

        verification = nil
        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          account.save!
          user.account = account
          user.save!
          account.update!(owner: user)
          verification = EmailVerification.issue_for(user)
        end

        AccountMailer.email_verification(user, verification.raw_token).deliver_now

    actual = normalize_origin(origin, allow_path: false)
    expected.present? && actual.present? && actual == expected
  end

    raw.empty? ? DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM : raw

    query = URI.encode_www_form(account: account.subdomain, token: token)

    query = URI.encode_www_form(account: account.subdomain, token: token)
    "#{frontend_url}/reset-password?#{query}"

  def normalize_origin(value, allow_path:)
    return nil if value.blank?

    uri = URI.parse(value.to_s.strip)
    return nil unless uri.scheme && uri.host
    return nil if uri.userinfo.present?

    unless allow_path
      return nil unless uri.path.blank? && uri.query.nil? && uri.fragment.nil?
    end

    scheme = uri.scheme.downcase
    return nil unless %w[http https].include?(scheme)

    host = uri.host.downcase
    default_port = (scheme == "https" ? 443 : 80)
    port_part = (uri.port && uri.port != default_port) ? ":#{uri.port}" : ""
    "#{scheme}://#{host}#{port_part}"
  rescue URI::InvalidURIError
    nil
  end

  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze

  belongs_to :account

    status == "open"
  end

  def pending?
    status == "pending"
  end

  def solved?
    status == "solved"
  end
